previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for right upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and fever. The pain resolved during the hospital stay, and imaging showed no acute abdominal pathology. A urine culture grew E. coli resistant to multiple antibiotics, prompting treatment with IV ertapenem. A midline catheter was placed to facilitate outpatient antibiotic administration. The patient's INR was subtherapeutic at 1.4, so bridging with Lovenox was initiated. She remained stable, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with a plan for seven days of IV antibiotics, anticoagulation management, and outpatient follow-up for urology and possible MRCP for recurrent abdominal pain.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old female with HIV well controlled on anti-retrovirals 
and multiple medical issues including morbid obesity, chronic 
pain, and opiate dependence presenting with 2 day h/o 
nausea/vomiting, diarrhea, and abdominal pain.  

ACTIVE:
# Abdominal pain: Possible gastroenteritis given sick contact 
and associated nausea and vomiting. However, given multiple 
prior presentations, description of crampy RUQ pain and LFT 
abnormalities in cholestatic patter, common duct stone possible 
although pt is s/p CCY. Given patient's body habitus, will defer 
RUQ ultrasound in favor of MRCP. MRCP was obtained but the 
patient left AMA prior to results being obtained.  

# Diarrhea - Gastroenteritis vs opiate withdrawal vs C diff 
given recent meropenem use. C. Diff assay was ordered but never 
obtained as the patient diarrhea resolved with the reassumption 
of PO medication and no stool was sent. 

# Positive UA- h/o recurrent resistant UTIs.  Will defer 
antibiotic therapy for now as pt likely colonized with resistant 
E coli and this may not represent active infection (+ dysuria 
when asked, no fevers, leukocytosis).  Urine culture was 
obtained but the patient left AMA prior to the results of the 
urine Cx returning. The urine culture grew out pan-sensitive 
PROTEUS MIRABILIS and the patient will need to be contacted and 
antibiotics.  Given the patients allergy history and the urine 
cx, Bactrim could be used to treat the uncomplicated UTI. 

# Recent Rape: Pt mentioned to nursing that she had been raped 
in the last 2 weeks, but declines to discuss the incident 
further. Seen by social work and discussed matter. Per report 
the patient had reported this to the police prior to coming into 
the hospital.. Urine HCG negative ___. Urine chlamydia pcr 
negative. Declined discussing the event with MD team. 

CHRONIC:
# chronic pain / methadone use - Pt on 110 mg methadone daily 
which she has not been able to take for 2 days prior to 
presentation to the hospital in the setting of nausea/vomiting. 
While pt is hypertensive (note not tachycardic) with diarrhea 
n/v/ and abd pain- sx consistent with opiate w/withdrawal - all 
of these have another explanation and proceeded the 
discontinuation of methadone. Methadone withdrawal is now likely 
superimposed upon underlying etiology.  These symptoms resolved 
with the patient able to tolerate PO medication and symptoms 
improved. 
 
# HTN to 180s in ED, likely ___ pain and/or narcotic withdrawal. 
The patient remained normotensive on the floor on her home 
medications.
 
# HIV (CD4>1000, undetectable viral load in ___. She was 
continued on her home HAART medications. 
 
# h/o DVT - on Coumadin. INR low at 1.6 on admission. She was 
continued on her home dose of Coumadin while in the hospital. 

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES:
The patient's MRCP is pending read and will need to be followed 
up on. In addition the patient's Urine Cx was pending at time of 
the patient leaving AMA and the patient will need to be 
contacted to provide treatment. In addition while the patient 
was in the hospital she repeatedly expressed depressive thoughts 
with regards to her loss of her mother. She also lamented her 
deteriorating health and her lack of support. All of these items 
leave her at risk for readmission. In addition the patient left 
AMA despite the team's multiple attempts to rationalize with her 
why she was in the hospital.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  HIV.  History of distant cholecystectomy presenting with recurrent
colicky right upper quadrant pain.  ? stone.  

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar T1 and T2 weighted images were acquired on a 1.5 tesla
magnet including dynamic 3D imaging obtained prior to, during and after the
uneventful intravenous administration of 17 mL of Gadavist.  

FINDINGS:

The patient is status post cholecystectomy.  There is mild prominence of the
common bile duct and central intrahepatic ducts, with the common bile duct
measuring 0.8 cm in diameter.  However, this is within normal limits in a
patient that is status post cholecystectomy.  No filling defects are
identified within the biliary tree. 

The liver has a nodular contour and the caudate lobe is enlarged, consistent
with cirrhosis.  There is signal loss in the liver between the in-phase and
out-of-phase sequences consistent with hepatic steatosis. No focal liver
lesions. The portal and hepatic veins are patent. The hepatic artery is patent
with conventional hepatic arterial anatomy. There are two mildly enlarged
portocaval lymph nodes, measuring up to 1 cm in short axis diameter (se 6 im
21 and se 15 im 52).

There is splenomegaly with the spleen measuring 14.7 cm in length. The spleen
is otherwise unremarkable.  Pancreas divisum is noted. The pancreas is
otherwise unremarkable. The pancreatic duct is of normal caliber.
Subcentimeter simple cysts are noted within the right kidney. The kidneys are
otherwise unremarkable.  There are single renal arteries bilaterally. 

The adrenals are within normal limits. The visualized small and large bowel is
unremarkable. No retroperitoneal or mesenteric adenopathy. 

There is a compression fracture at T8 with approximately 50% loss of vertebral
body height - this is unchanged since the previous CT in ___. There is
also collapse of the superior vertebral endplate at L3 which is also unchanged
since ___. A Schmorl's node is noted within the superior vertebral endplate
of L1. The L4 and L5 vertebral bodies are fused. No destructive osseous
lesions. 

IMPRESSION:

1. No evidence of biliary obstruction. Mild prominence of the central
intrahepatic and extrahepatic ducts which is within normal limits post
cholecystectomy. 

2. Cirrhotic liver. Mild splenomegaly which is likely secondary to portal
hypertension. Mild-moderate hepatic steatosis. 

3. Pancreas divisum.

4. Chronic compression fracture at T8 and superior vertebral endplate collapse
at L3.
